facts.statement: The genus Gavialosuchus was described by Toula and Kail in 1885.
Gavialosuchus lived in Europe during the early Miocene.
facts.quote: Gavialosuchus is an extinct genus of gavialoid crocodylian from the early Miocene of Europe.

facts.statement: The type species Gavialosuchus eggenburgensis is known from the early Miocene of Austria.
facts.quote: The type species, G. eggenburgensis, is known from the early Miocene of Austria.

facts.statement: Two other species, G. americanus and G. carolinensis, have been reclassified into other genera.
facts.quote: Two other species - G. americanus and G. carolinensis - have since been reclassified to other genera.

facts.statement: A 2012 study by Brochu and Storrs found strong support for the suggestion that G. americanus and G. carolinensis belong to the genus Thecachampsa.
facts.quote: Christopher A. Brochu and Glenn W. Storrs (2012) tested all four species, along with other crocodyloids, and found relatively strong support for Piras et al. (2007) suggestion.

facts.statement: A 2018 study by Weems agreed that G. americanus and G. carolinensis are part of the genus Thecachampsa.
facts.quote: Weems (2018) agreed with Piras et al. (2007) and Brochu & Storrs (2012) at americanus and carolinensis are part of Thecachampsa.

facts.statement: Recent molecular studies indicate that tomistomines, including Gavialosuchus, belong to Gavialoidea rather than being crocodiles.
facts.quote: Based on morphological studies of extinct taxa, the tomistomines (including the living false gharial) were long thought to be classified as crocodiles and not closely related to gavialoids. However, recent molecular studies using DNA sequencing have consistently indicated that the false gharial (Tomistoma) (and by inference other related extinct forms in Tomistominae) actually belong to Gavialoidea.

facts.statement: Gavialosuchus lived in eastern North America during the late Oligocene and Miocene, and in Europe during the Miocene.
facts.quote: Gavialosuchus es un género extinto de crocodiliano tomistomino extinto del Oligoceno superior y el Mioceno del este de América del Norte y el Mioceno de Europa.

facts.statement: G. carolinensis could reach 5.37 meters in length, while a specimen of G. americanus is estimated to have reached 9.75 meters based on a skull measuring 132 centimeters.
facts.quote: G. carolinensispodía alcanzar 5.37 metros de longitud, y se estima que un espécimen de G. americanus alcanzaba 9.75 metros de largo, basándose en su cráneo que mide unos 132 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: Unlike modern freshwater relatives, Gavialosuchus was an estuarine and coastal crocodilian living in shallow marine waters.
facts.quote: A diferencia de sus parientes modernos de agua dulce, Gavialosuchus era un crocodiliano estuarino y de zonas costeras, viviendo en aguas marinas superficiales junto al sirenio Metaxytherium, el platanístido Pomatodelphis, y el tiburón Hemipristis serra.

facts.statement: The time range for Gavialosuchus is from the Chattian to the Tortonian, between 27.3 and 7.246 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Chattian to Tortonian (27.3 to 7.246 million years ago)

facts.statement: The classification of Gavialosuchus remains an unresolved issue.
facts.quote: Como ocurre con muchos taxones extintos, la clasificación de Gavialosuchus es una cuestión sin resolver.
